In the LINE paper (Tang et al., 2015), LINE(2nd), which models second-order proximity (similarity of vertices' neighborhood or context distributions), generally performs better than LINE(1st) on word analogy tasks. First-order proximity captures direct edge-level co-occurrence, which is a weaker signal for analogy relations, whereas second-order proximity captures shared contexts, which better supports analogical structure. Combining the two orders (concatenating the embeddings) is reported to improve over either alone.
